comment: ID tokens carry roles, groups and permissions whatever the scope. A recorded design choice: applications authorize on them without a UserInfo call (docs/OAUTH-OIDC.md, "What a scope actually buys").

When the email scope is granted, the ID token carries email and email_verified as well as UserInfo. Core §5.4 lets the server return them from UserInfo; putting them in the ID token too is a recorded choice (docs/OAUTH-OIDC.md, Known deviations).
The same choice as oidcc-scope-email: with the email scope, the ID token carries email and email_verified.

The profile scope returns name, given_name, family_name and preferred_username, not the other standard profile claims (picture, locale, zoneinfo and the rest), which OpenIDX does not store (docs/OAUTH-OIDC.md, Known deviations).
OpenIDX does not support the claims request parameter, which Core §5.5 makes optional, so an essential claim it asks for is not added (docs/OAUTH-OIDC.md, Known deviations).
UserInfo accepts the access token only in the Authorization header. Accepting it in a form body (RFC 6750 §2.2) is to be added; remove this entry with that fix.
No acr claim is returned when acr_values is sent (Core §3.1.2.1 says SHOULD). To be added; remove this entry with that fix.

current-block: Testing if access token was revoked after authorization code reuse (the AS 'should' have revoked the access token)
comment: A replayed code is refused, but the access token already issued from it is not revoked (RFC 6749 §4.1.2 says SHOULD). To be added; remove this entry with that fix.
